pr_title: udevadm: wait: check if specified path not exist on --remove
pr_body:
Even if the corresponding device node or syspath are already removed,
the specified symlink to the device node may still exist.

Fixes #23166.
pr_comments: or in other words, this has a certain TTOCTTOU feel to it... why do we need to check in advance what sd-device_new_from_path() should be able to figure out on its own? Can you elaborate?

@poettering The issue here is, when a user specified a symlink to a device node, the previous logic may allow `udevadm wait --removed` being finished even though the symlink still exists, though in that case the symlink is broken or dangling. Why? When `check_device()` is called, the device node and/or the corresponding syspath may be already removed (hence, `sd_device_new_from_path()` fails with -ENODEV), but udevd may not processed the 'remove' uevent yet.

On `--removed`, checking the specified path with `laccess()` ensures the symlink not exist anymore. Of course, still there may be a chance that udevd is still processing the corresponding 'remove' uevent, but we can avoid the chance by setting `--settle` option.
